issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims the lower bound b_Gamma(v_f,v_r,w_s; v_f,0) >= C*eps*||v_f||_{1,Omega_S}^2 + eps^{-1} sum_E h_E^{-1}||n_S.v_f + n_P.v_r + n_P.w_s||_{0,E}^2. But b_Gamma(v_f,v_r,w_s; v_f,0) = -int_Sigma 2*mu_f((eps(v_f)n_S).n_S)(n_S.v_f + n_P.v_r + n_P.w_s) ds is a sign-indefinite cross term: for any v_h in the subspace V_{h,0} defined in the proof of Lemma inf_sup (nonzero discrete velocities with vanishing normal combination on Sigma) the left-hand side is exactly 0 while the claimed right-hand side is >= C*eps*||v_f||_{1,Omega_S}^2 > 0. The displayed ellipticity step is therefore false as written; the individual inequalities listed are never combined into a lower bound for the full block operator A (x^T A x), and the cross-coupling terms (rho_f*phi, -theta, BJS couplings between u_r, y_s and u_s) are never absorbed. The parameter conditions on gamma and eps_hat_f' in the theorems show the intended Young-absorption argument, which is not carried out.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the b_Gamma cross term by a weighted Young inequality of the type already displayed in (I1), absorb the eps_hat_f'-weighted trace term into a_f^S, and dominate the h_E^{-1}-weighted remainder by the Nitsche term c_Gamma under the condition gamma > (1+varsigma)(eps_hat_f')^{-1}; then combine all block contributions (using the stated two-sided bound for the rho_f*phi mass combination) into x^T A x >= c||x||^2. All stated results survive with these constants.
issues.overall_effect: The ellipticity of the block operator A, which underpins the kernel characterization (Lemma invertibilty), the invertibility of M+N (Lemma invertibilty1), the well-posedness results (Theorems E+H, thm:added-1, thm:added-2), and the stability and error estimates that invoke Lemma coercivity-continuity, is unestablished.
issues.title: False lower bound for the interface form b_Gamma in the ellipticity proof of Lemma coercivity-continuity
issues.why_classification: The repair is the standard, contained Nitsche Young-absorption argument whose parameter conditions already appear in the theorem statements; no new proof architecture is needed and no advertised result is lost, but the false displayed inequality is not a routine typo since a premise must be reorganized.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma usual_inf is stated with the supremum over the full space V_h. The proof of Lemma inf_sup needs the same lower bound with the supremum restricted to the proper subspace V_{h,0} (functions whose normal components satisfy the interface constraint); a supremum over a proper subspace is not bounded below by the full-space inf-sup constant, so the chain sup_{V_h} >= sup_{V_{h,0}} >= xi_1 (hence xi_2) ||q|| is an invalid inference. The constrained inf-sup with the interface terms C_{*,Gamma} present is precisely the nontrivial content and is not established.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove the inf-sup condition for the augmented B directly, e.g. by a Fortin-type construction whose corrector respects the interface constraint, or bound the interface term with the h_E-weighted trace estimate (I2) and dominate it with the Nitsche penalty; the constant xi_2 then follows with the stated structure.
issues.overall_effect: The LBB condition for the operator B (including the interface terms) is unproven; consequently the pressure-uniqueness step of Theorem E+H, the kernel statement for B^T in Lemma invertibilty (and via it Lemma invertibilty1), and the pressure bounds in Lemma lem:added-1 and Theorem appendix_fully are unsupported.
issues.title: Inf-sup proof for the augmented constraint block invalidly restricts the supremum to a subspace
issues.why_classification: A contained, known-type construction (Fortin operator or penalty-aided estimate) restores the lemma without new proof architecture or loss of any stated guarantee, but it is more than a routine local edit, so the issue is moderate.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma is stated and immediately used, but no proof is given anywhere in the source. Moreover the block factorization on which such a proof would rest does not match the displayed matrices: the (5,1) entry of M+N is -(B^S)^* + (C_{f,Gamma})^* (from the displayed N), while the displayed factorization M+N = [[A, B^T],[-B, C]] requires -(B^S)^* - (C_{f,Gamma})^* there; the (5,2), (5,3) entries of the constraint block carry + signs where the factorization gives minus signs. Hence even the premise needed to transfer the kernel conditions of Lemma invertibilty to M+N is not established by the displayed identities.

failure_location.quote: if the matrices $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{C}$ are positive semi-definite and $\operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{A}) \cap \operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{B}) = \operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{C}) \cap \operatorname{ker}(\mathbf{B}^T) = \{0\}$, then the matrix $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$ is invertible for any given $ \bw_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S}} \in \mathbf{K}_h$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the block decomposition of M+N with consistent signs, then supply the short standard argument: if (M+N)(u,p)=0, the two block equations give u^T A u + p^T C p = 0 after multiplying by u^T and p^T and adding, whence u = 0 by the positive definiteness of A's quadratic form and p in ker(C) cap ker(B^T) = {0}; the same argument covers the pencil sM+N for s > 0.
issues.overall_effect: The invertibility of the DAE matrix M+N (the existence step of Theorem E+H) and, transitively, the well-posedness results built on it (Theorems E+H, thm:added-1, thm:added-2) are unsupported.
issues.title: Lemma invertibilty1 asserts invertibility of M+N without any proof, and its supporting block decomposition is inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A complete resolution requires correcting matrix entries and adding a nontrivial (though standard) invertibility argument; the result and all its uses survive, so the issue is moderate rather than minor or serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: According to the DAE theory (see \cite[Theorem~2.3.1]{MR1101809}), if the matrix pencil \(s\,\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}\) is nonsingular for some \(s\neq 0\) and the initial data are consistent, then the system \eqref{mixed-primal} admits a solution.

issues.failure_explanation: The inference 'no zero rows implies no algebraic constraints' is false: algebraic constraints correspond to the singularity of M (zero columns), and the displayed M has an identically zero fifth column (the pressure p_h^S never appears with a time derivative; the fifth row is (0,0,(C_{s,Gamma})^*,0,0,0)). The paper itself calls (mixed-primal) a DAE. Consequently the premise 'the initial data are consistent' required by the invoked DAE theorem (Brenan-Campbell-Petzold, Thm. 2.3.1) is asserted ('are consistent and do not lead to any incompatibility issues') rather than verified: no algebraic constraint is identified and no compatibility of the prescribed initial data is checked; moreover the presence of d_tau y_s in the fluid-mass row makes the index analysis nontrivial.

failure_location.quote: The matrix \(E\) has no zero rows, which implies that the system has no algebraic constraints.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Identify the algebraic variable(s) and the induced constraint, verify (or impose) the consistency of the prescribed initial data with the hidden constraint(s), and reapply the DAE existence theorem (or replace it by the standard Galerkin/Oseen argument after eliminating the pressure via the inf-sup condition) within its hypotheses.
issues.overall_effect: The existence half of Theorem E+H (well-posedness of the linearized semi-discrete problem, hence of the fixed-point map J_h) is unsupported; the uniqueness argument is independent and survives.
issues.title: False DAE claim and unverified initial-data consistency in the existence proof of Theorem E+H
issues.why_classification: The gap is confined to the existence step of one proof; a correct, contained treatment of the DAE structure (index/consistency analysis) preserves the theorem as stated, so the issue is moderate, not serious.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: which together with the fact that $\bu_{f2,h}^{\mathrm{S}} \in \mathbf{K}_h$, allows us to assert the bounds

issues.failure_explanation: Banach's theorem is applied to J_h on K_h, but the only thing established beforehand is well-posedness of the linearized (Oseen/poroelastic) problem for each w in K_h; that the resulting solution's first component satisfies the defining bound of K_h is never proved, although the contraction estimate itself invokes 'u_{f2,h} in K_h', i.e. presupposes J_h(K_h) subset of K_h. The radius of K_h involves only ||f_S||, whereas the linearized solution's H^1-norm depends on all data (f_P, theta, r_S, initial data), so membership does not follow from the smallness of ||f_S|| alone; no a priori bound establishing the invariance is provided, and uniqueness is only obtained among fixed points in K_h.

issues.title: Fixed-point operator J_h is never shown to map K_h into itself (Theorem thm:added-1)
issues.why_classification: Closing the gap needs a genuine new estimate for the linearized system (a contained nontrivial argument) and possibly a weakened definition of K_h, but no new global proof architecture and no abandonment of the advertised well-posedness result; hence moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: then the matrix $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$ is invertible for any given $ \bw_{f,h}^{\mathrm{S}} \in \mathbf{K}_h$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims that scaling M by 1/tau and adding N gives a matrix with 'the same structure' as M+N, whose nonsingularity was 'shown in the proof of Lemma invertibilty'. Both claims fail: (i) the proof of Lemma invertibilty establishes only kernel intersections and never nonsingularity of M+N; the only statement asserting nonsingularity is Lemma invertibilty1, which carries no proof (see ISSUE-003); (ii) tau^{-1}M + N does not have the displayed saddle-point structure: the mass matrix contributes, e.g., (C_{s,Gamma})^*/tau to the (5,3) entry of the constraint block (M's fifth row is (0,0,(C_{s,Gamma})^*,0,0,0)), so the kernel/inf-sup conditions established for A, B, C do not transfer to the scaled pencil without an independent argument.

failure_location.quote: This resulting matrix has the same structure as $\mathbf{M} + \mathbf{N}$, which is shown to be nonsingular in the proof of Lemma~\ref{invertibilty}. Therefore, the scaled matrix is nonsingular, and so is the matrix in \eqref{mixed-primal}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove nonsingularity of L = (1/tau)M + N directly, e.g. by showing that the homogeneous scaled system has only the zero solution via the discrete energy structure (using the coercivity of A and the positive mass terms), or prove nonsingularity of the pencil sM+N for all s >= 1/tau; the assertion of Theorem thm:added-2 then holds as stated.
issues.overall_effect: The guarantee that each backward-Euler step is uniquely solvable is unproven; the stability analysis (lem:added-1) and the error theorem, which presuppose well-defined discrete solutions, rest on this unestablished solvability.
issues.title: Unique solvability of the backward-Euler system justified by a nonsingularity result that is never established (Theorem thm:added-2)
issues.why_classification: A correct direct proof of nonsingularity of the scaled matrix is a contained but genuine argument (the constraint block changes under scaling, so the analogy cannot simply be invoked); no advertised regime or rate is lost, so the issue is moderate.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and the additional scalar and vector terms $m_{\Sigma,\mathrm{ex}}^i$ (computed with the exact solutions \eqref{num} entail the following changes in the linear functionals)

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims that the inhomogeneous interface data m^i_{Sigma,ex} 'entail the following changes in the linear functionals' and displays the modified F. As displayed, these are not linear functionals of the stated test functions: the third term of F(v_f^S) is the fixed density (gamma*mu_f/h_E) m^1_{Sigma,ex} (2*mu_f*eps(u_f^S)) n_S n_S with no test function (a bare scalar, and it carries the Nitsche penalty weight that belongs to the mass term, not to the normal-stress term), and the first term of F(v_r^P) pairs the poroelastic load rho_f*phi*f_P with the fluid test function v_f^S instead of v_r^P. Hence the right-hand sides of the convergence test are not defined by the source as written, and the claimed validation of the theoretical rates (Table conv_test_space) is not reproducible as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Re-derive the consistency terms for the inhomogeneous interface data from the Nitsche formulation and rewrite each displayed F as a genuine linear functional of the corresponding test function (in particular pairing rho_f*phi*f_P with v_r^P and attaching the test function to the normal-stress consistency term).
issues.overall_effect: The convergence experiment of Section 6.1 is not well defined as specified; no formal theorem depends on it.
issues.title: Modified right-hand sides for the manufactured-solution test are not linear functionals as displayed
issues.why_classification: A local, contained correction of the displayed functionals restores the experiment; the method, its guarantees, and all formal results of the paper are unaffected, so the issue is minor.
